title: Applied ML Evals: End-to-End Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
# Applied ML Evals: End-to-End Playbook

Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended processes for evaluation (eval) harness usage, prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profile validation, and regression triage. It is intended for ML Engineers, Applied ML, and Platform teams who are onboarding models to the Redwood serving stack or maintaining production quality.

Scope:
- Covers automated eval harness workflows, prompt set management, benchmark design, model onboarding checklist, quality guardrails, quantization validation, and regression triage procedures.
- Focused on model types used in the Redwood catalog (decoder-only and encoder-decoder open models) for text generation, chat, and embeddings.
- Excludes low-level kernel optimization and hardware provisioning (see eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture).

Owners & Responsibilities:
- Applied ML (primary): owns eval harness, prompt sets, and quality metrics.
- Model Onboarding squad (secondary): executes onboarding checklist, performance/latency validation.
- Serving Runtime & Infra: provides perf metrics, KV cache and batching instrumentation.
- Product/Customer Success: supply representative prompt traces for customer-facing workloads.

1) Eval Harness: standard configuration and CI integration
- Purpose: run deterministic, repeatable evals against model candidates and deployed model variants.
- Location: eval-harness repo + CI job (see pipeline: ci/evals/run-eval-suite.yaml).
- Standard config parameters (example table):

| key | description | recommended default | notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| eval_name | human readable id | regression-smoke | used to map to dashboards |
| model_id | model artifact or container tag | model-vX.Y | must match model catalog entry |
| dataset_id | prompt set or benchmark id | credit-card-redaction-2025 | stored in prompt-sets catalog |
| metrics | list of metrics to compute | perplexity,accuracy,f1,bert_score | include qualitative evals for chat |
| seeds | random seeds for determinism | [0,1,2] | use identical seeds across runs |

- CI Integration: every change to a model-serving image, inference config, or prompt set must trigger the eval-harness CI job for the affected baselines.
- Reporting: eval results are emitted to the eval-results S3 prefix and a summary is posted to the eval dashboard (Tooling: eval-dashboard.redwood.internal).

2) Prompt Sets & Benchmarks: organization and governance
- Naming convention: <domain>-<intent>-<version> (e.g., customer-support-refactor-2026-v1).
- Ownership: each prompt set must have an owner and a documented source (customer trace, public benchmark, or synthetic generator).
- Metadata required for each prompt set (stored in the prompt-sets catalog): owner, description, intended model capabilities, dataset size, sensitive-content flags, acceptance thresholds.
- Prompt diversity: ensure coverage for short vs long context, multi-turn chat, instruction-following, and adversarial cases.
- Benchmark design checklist:
  1. Define clear task and success criteria.
  2. Partition into training/validation/holdout where applicable.
  3. Annotate expected outputs and, for generative tasks, multiple acceptable references.
  4. Indicate whether prompts contain PII or regulated content.

3) Model Onboarding Guide (short checklist)
Follow these steps for each new model variant introduced to the platform:
1. Sanity & unit checks: model loads, tokenizer alignment, sample inference for short/long contexts.
2. Eval harness run: run standard eval suite (smoke + task-specific benchmarks).
3. Performance profiling: latency p50/p95, GPU memory, token throughput measured via benchmarking-and-perf-suite.
4. Cost & quantization assessment: run quantization profile (see section 6) and measure quality delta.
5. Safety & guardrails test: run quality guardrails and safety prompts (toxic, hallucination checks).
6. Canary rollout: small % of production traffic (0.5% -> 5% -> 25%) with close monitoring of SLOs and quality metrics.
7. Post-launch regression eval: run full eval suite daily during the first week and weekly thereafter.

Each step must be recorded in the model onboarding ticket template and linked to the model catalog entry.

4) Quality Guardrails & Acceptance Criteria
- Purpose: prevent quality regressions and ensure safe outputs for customer workloads.
- Core categories and example checks:
  - Correctness: task-specific metrics (accuracy/F1/ROUGE), semantic similarity thresholds (embedding cosine >= 0.80).
  - Consistency: response stability across seeds and minimal variance in structured outputs.
  - Safety: toxic content detection (score thresholds), PII leakage detection.
  - Latency & Availability: p95 latency <= 400ms for n-1 models on Dedicated; availability >= 99.9% per SLA.
- Thresholds table (examples):

| metric | alert threshold | block threshold | action |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| accuracy (task-X) | drop >5% relative to baseline | drop >10% | if block -> rollback canary & open incident |
| embedding cosine | drop >0.03 abs | drop >0.07 abs | schedule urgent triage |
| toxicity score | >0.6 (10% of samples) | >0.75 (any flagged high-risk sample) | pause rollouts, notify security |
| p95 latency | increase >20% | increase >40% | scale up dedicated pool or rollback |

- Automated checks: eval harness includes pre-commit checks for prompt-set changes and post-deploy weekly evaluation jobs that run nightly.

5) Regression Triage Playbook (when an eval fails)
1. Triage owner assignment: the oncall Applied ML engineer is assigned within 15 minutes.
2. Data collection: gather the failing eval run id, model artifact, git commit hash, inference config, hardware type, and recent infra events.
3. Compare to baseline: compute diff of metric deltas and sample-level failures.
4. Classify regression type:
   - Data/Prompt drift: prompts changed or production prompt distribution shifted.
   - Model quality regression: model weights/quantization caused accuracy loss.
   - Inference bug/regression: tokenizer mismatch, decoding bug, memory corruption.
   - Infrastructure induced: GPU throttle, CUDA error, networking blips.
5. Mitigation actions by class:
   - Data drift: revert prompt set, notify product teams, create new prompt coverage.
   - Model quality: rollback to last good model tag, schedule re-quantization.
   - Inference bug: hotfix to runtime, trigger CI job, block rollouts.
   - Infra: scale/replace nodes, investigate kernel logs.
6. Postmortem: if regression triggers a blocked threshold or customer impact, follow incident postmortem process (oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems).

6) Quantization Profiles & Validation
- Purpose: reduce cost while bounding quality delta.
- Profile components:
  - Quantization config id (e.g., q4_0_int8-ops-2026-v1).
  - Target hardware (A100, H100, triton-inference), supported ops list.
  - Expected memory savings and throughput gain.
- Validation steps:
  1. Run quantize job with representative dataset (prompt set).
  2. Compute quality delta across primary metrics (must meet acceptance thresholds from section 4).
  3. Run stress perf test for long-context behavior and KV cache correctness.
  4. Measure CPU/GPU memory and OOM rates for long tails.
  5. Produce quantization report and approved signoff (owner + applied-ml lead).
- Allowed deltas: default max allowed quality drop is 3% absolute on primary task metrics unless approved by product.

7) Runbook: evaluating a new model candidate (step-by-step)
1. Create model onboarding ticket and link model artifact to the model catalog.
2. Run lint/sanity tests: tokenizer consistency, model-output schema checks.
3. Execute eval harness: smoke tests + full benchmark suite.
4. Review eval dashboard and diff against baseline model.
5. If within acceptance, proceed to quantization profiling; otherwise iterate or reject.
6. Complete safety checks and generate canary config.
7. Coordinate with infra to schedule canary and configure routing rules (percentages, fallback policies).
8. Monitor during canary for 72 hours with automated rollback triggers enabled.

8) Metrics, Dashboards and Alerts (practical guidance)
- Important metrics to surface: task accuracy, embedding cosine, toxicity rate, hallucination indicators (e.g., hallucination_score), token-level latency p50/p95, error rates (5xx), OOM occurrences.
- Dashboards: per-model & per-prompt-set dashboards. Use tags to group models by architecture and quantization profile.
- Alerts: configure alerting for the thresholds in section 4 with playbook links embedded in the alert description.

9) Examples & CLI snippets
- Eval harness run example (CLI):
  eval-run --config configs/evals/credit-card-redaction.yaml --model model-v2.1 --seeds 0,1,2 --out s3://eval-results/2026-01-01-run

- Minimal model onboarding ticket template (fields):
  - model_id
  - artifact_tag
  - owner
  - oncall_contact
  - eval_suite_run_id
  - perf_profile_id
  - quant_profile_id
  - canary_config_link

10) FAQs & Common Gotchas
- Q: "We see different outputs between local and CI runs"
  A: Ensure identical tokenizer, random seed, and sampling params. CI uses deterministic seeds and fixed sampling settings; local runs often omit these.
- Q: "Quantized model shows higher latency"
  A: Verify kernel selection and backend; sometimes lower-bit kernels have different scheduling overhead. Check runtime kernel logs and throughput tests.
